# Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We want Rinchen to be a place where anyone can take part without fear of harassment. This holds for every contributor, maintainer and user, whatever their age, body size, disability (visible or not), ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, experience, education, economic background, nationality, appearance, race, religion, sexual identity and orientation, or first language.

Many people here care about Mongolian, and many do not write English as a first language. We pledge to be patient with questions, to welcome contributions written in clear, simple English, and to accept help from people who use assistive technology.

We act and interact in ways that build an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive and healthy community.

## Our standards

Behavior that helps the community:

- Being kind and patient with people at every level of experience.
- Respecting other points of view and other ways of working.
- Giving feedback that is specific and constructive, and receiving it with grace.
- Owning a mistake, apologizing to the people it affected, and learning from it.
- Thinking about what is best for the whole community, not only for oneself.

Behavior that is not acceptable:

- Sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind.
- Insults, derogatory comments, trolling, and personal or political attacks.
- Harassment in public or in private, including repeated unwanted contact.
- Publishing someone's private information, such as a home or email address, without their explicit permission.
- Mocking someone's English, their Mongolian, or the way they use the tools they need.
- Any other conduct that would be out of place in a professional setting.

## Responsibilities of the maintainers

The maintainers explain what acceptable behavior is, and they act fairly and promptly when behavior falls short of it.

They may remove, edit or reject comments, commits, code, Wiki edits, issues and other contributions that do not follow this Code of Conduct, and they will say why when that is appropriate. They respect the privacy and the safety of anyone who reports a problem.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies in every space the project runs: this repository (issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions and the Wiki) and any place where someone speaks for the project in public, such as a talk or a post made on its behalf.

It also applies when someone's behavior outside those spaces harms a member of the community inside them.

## Enforcement

Unacceptable behavior may be reported to the maintainer, who enforces this Code of Conduct. Every report is reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly. The identity of the person who reports is kept private.

### Reporting

To report a problem, write to bbattseren88@gmail.com. Say what happened, where (a link helps), when, and who was involved. We aim to reply within 7 days.

You can also use GitHub's own tools: see [GitHub's guide to reporting abuse or spam](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam). If your report is about the maintainer, use GitHub's tools instead of email, so that someone other than the person concerned reads it.

## Enforcement guidelines

The maintainer follows these four steps and starts with the one that fits the harm done.

### Correction

**Impact:** Behavior that was out of place or unwelcome, with no intent to harm.

**Consequence:** A private, written note that explains what was wrong and why. A public apology may be asked for.

### Warning

**Impact:** A violation in a single event, or a pattern of smaller ones over time.

**Consequence:** A written warning that says what must stop. There is no contact with the people involved for an agreed period, and that includes the spaces of the project and any outside channel. Breaking those terms can lead to a temporary or a permanent ban.

### Temporary ban

**Impact:** A serious violation, or behavior that continues after a warning.

**Consequence:** A ban from every space of the project for an agreed period, with no public or private contact with the people involved. Breaking those terms can lead to a permanent ban.

### Permanent ban

**Impact:** A pattern of violations, harassment of a person, or aggression toward or contempt for a group of people.

**Consequence:** A permanent ban from every space of the project.
